summary: self-sign ships a PEM-disguised eval() backdoor in its main entry point
details: index.js's exported generate(attrs, options, defaults) function accepts a third argument, strips `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` / `-----END CERTIFICATE-----` framing and whitespace, base64-decodes the remaining body, and passes the result to eval(), with the call wrapped in a try/catch that swallows errors. The library advertises only X.509 self-signed certificate generation and none of its documented behavior requires evaluating caller-supplied data; the PEM envelope disguises executable JavaScript as certificate content. Any caller that supplies a PEM-shaped string as the third argument to generate() executes arbitrary JavaScript in the host Node.js process. The manifest name `self-sign` also diverges from the README, CHANGELOG, and JSDoc, which consistently identify the library as `selfsign` (`npm install selfsign`, `require('selfsign')`), and a `package.json.bak` at version 5.5.0 preserves the same identity mismatch — consistent with a name-squat republish of the upstream `selfsign` package carrying the added eval trampoline.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
